sections.text: Content with what comes to him without effort of his own, mounting above the pairs of opposites, free from envy, his mind balanced both in success and failure; though he acts, yet the consequences do not bind him.
He who is without attachment, free, his mind centered in wisdom, his actions, being done as a sacrifice, leave no trace behind.

For him, the sacrifice itself is the Spirit; the Spirit and the oblation are one; it is the Spirit Itself which is sacrificed in Its own fire, and the man even in action is united with God, since while performing his act, his mind never ceases to be fixed on Him.

So we had been discussing chapter four, Gnana Karma Sannyasi Yoga. Yoga of Renouncing actions in Knowledge. So far we have seen that actions are necessary, but actions are also binding. My ultimate goal is to get happiness only way I feel happiness.
Im completely liberated from my limitations and here I am acting in this world and actions are binding. So what is the prescription? What is that one yoga which will liberate me from these limitations? So in the beginning Bhagavan said, this is the yoga which I taught from time immemorial to people. And people have been benefited by this by practicing this yoga to release themselves from these bondages.
So Im going to teach you again and see, the technique is very, very simple. You have to end all your actions in knowledge that you are not the actor. It is as simple as that.
Right now we are taking burden upon ourselves of something which does not belong to us, a responsibility which does not belong to me. Im taking upon myself which is to control the Karmaphala. My constant goal in life is to get the desired results.
Thats why we plan five year plan, three year plan. People ask me all the time, Rajan, whats your plan? I say, what do you mean whats my plan? Im talking about retirement. Whats your plan for retirement? You have to plan out retirement in a particular manner so that then I can enjoy the retirement.
So we plan our actions, keeping the final results in mind, which is Karma Phala. Karma Phala by very nature is not in my hand because Im not the Karma Falada. The rest of the world is the Karma Falada.
I act and the world react and that burden on me is binding me. Bhagawan said, once you realize that you are not the actor, the one who you think you are. This body, mind and intellect is not the one who you try to satisfy.
The one which is seeking happiness is someone other than your body, mind and intellect. One who wants to be liberated is someone other than your body, mind and intellect. So he starts out by giving his identity, say Ajaha, a peace on Abhyatma.
I myself is unborn, deathless, immutable, and also do not take part in any actions. And therefore the karmas dont bind me. The actions which I dont take part in, they cannot bind me.
Bhagavan said, at the macrocosm I am the all pervading Brahman who is infinite, unborn, deathless. And at the micro level Atman has the exact same quality. So at the macro level he is Brahmandu, all pervading, Almighty, all potent, omniscient God.
At a macro level is Myself which I constantly refer. I is nothing but his own Self. We have logically deducted in our discussion that this world cannot be separate from Him.
Because when he created this universe, the cosmos, the Brahman, no other material available to him other than his own Self created out of his own Self. And therefore you and I and this world cannot be any separate from Him. But that understanding when it takes place that this room space is no different than the space outside, then all the limitations of the room space will be gone.
So right now the room space thinks its limited by its wall, floor and ceiling, and it is suffering from its limitation. I want this room to have a higher ceiling. These limitations are also nothing but his own manifestation. If God is omnipresent, where is my body, my intellect, my mind? They are also part of Him. There is only one material available to him to create this universe, which is his own self.
So he created out of his own self. And now Im trying to liberate his self from these limitations which are also part of his self. It is like a cup which is made up of ice is immersed into water.
So the water outside the cup is also water. Water inside the cup is also water. And the cup itself is nothing but water.
But the crystallization creates identification of name and form and shape. The ego is that crystallization of the shape of a cup. When it melts, it will be all water.
So Bhagavan said, once you start realizing that the self you are trying to liberate is already liberated, it is not taking part in any of your actions and therefore it is not bound by it. But you are now identifying this self with this limited body, mind and intellect, with his name, forms and colors. And therefore you are reflecting all its limitations.
So he said, now you start contemplating on it and then live your life. We have seen that how to live life is Vitaraga Bhayakrodha -- without any attachment, without any particular desired fruits of actions which I had been trying to achieve, which are not in my hand. According to your swadharma.
We have learned Swadharma. This body has its own Swadharma. Mind has its own swadharma.
Intellect own swadharma. Just go with that flow. If I try to make this hall into a concert hall, Ill be disappointed.
It does not have any of the qualities of a concert hall. I try to have a music party and then I say I dont sound good here. Because the hall does not have the quality to have the acoustics of a concert hall.
As long as I live with the limitations of this room, Ill be happy with this room. As soon as I get out of my expectations of what this hall can do. Ill be disappointed.
Bhagavan said, follow your Svadharma and do actions without any attachment, without any particular expectation of the fruits of actions. So the last verse, the 22nd, describes the state you should be achieving to be perfectly happy. The stage which you have to achieve is Yadruchanthusthaha.
Content with whatever comes to you without effort. That sounds a little tricky to understand. It does not mean that you didnt put in your efforts.
But it means: without conniving and manipulating to control the results, without scheming so that everything will fall in place exactly as you want. Thats not going to happen. The results are not in your hand, no matter how smart you are.
Therefore, you act according to your dharma. Then whatever comes -- without manipulating outcomes -- you accept contentedly. You put your efforts.
You realize that was according to my efforts. Move on to the next step. Yadruchala va santoshta Dvanda Athitaha.
Of course we know that there are times that will be conducive. At time the fruits will be not conducive. I expected something.
I was targeting to achieve this. But I end up getting this. So thats going to happen.
Thats a given that the law of nature that things will be different every time, same effort. You put two different times, get two different results. Last time I said this and everybody was very excited.
And this time I said lets do this. And nobody is excited. So the world will be like that.
Therefore, you will be buffeted between hope and dejection. Vimatsaraha without envy. Now this sounds very difficult.
But it is the only way you can be happy, because as you have seen in our analogies, somebody will always be a little better than me no matter how high I go. I saw on CNBC someplace that the most difficult group of people to plan retirement for is millionaires. Its easier for someone in the hundred thousand range.
They can project how many times your current income you need for retirement. Its easy for a guy making $60,000 a year. Guys making $10 million a year -- theyre very difficult.
You see, its very difficult as you go higher and higher to achieve that perfection. Bill Gates -- if you tell him he needs an income seven times his current income to retire, he will never be able to retire. So Bhagavan said, Vimatsarah: do not judge your situation by comparing with the other person.
You do not know his situation. Every time I see Facebook, I get very depressed because everybody else in the world seems so happy. Im the only one who has all these responsibilities and problems.
Do not compare your situation with others. Thats where the envy comes. I stopped reading Fortune and Bloomberg and Newsweek because it depresses me.
Vimatsaraha -- Bhagwan said, the only way to be happy is not to compare your situation with others. Sama Siddhava Siddha, we know success and failure. Its a relative term.
But you decided what success is and you did what failure is. You remember that whatever really came is what you really deserved. Used to say, you dont get what you desire, you get what you deserve.
Sama Siddha ashidhav krutvapi nani badhyata. He never gets bound by any actions he performs, good, bad or ugly. Because once you perform actions youre done with, theres nothing you can do about it.
So whatever comes back, you say, okay, next move, lets go to the next one. So you see, thats the state you need to achieve. And it seems very difficult, but it is truly, Ill tell you, it is the only way you will be happy.
When you get closer to that state, it may not be exactly as you imagine in your mind what yogi should be. But at some level, you have to achieve this to be happy. So next verse says, gatha sangasya muktasya gnana avasthi da cha yajnaya acharataha Karma Samagram Praviliyate.
Our goal right from the beginning was not to be bound by my actions. My actions should be always pristine and come with the results which are complete. So I will never have to be reacting to it.
So I dont want to be bound by my actions. So the first goal we have said is Gata Sangasya. Attachment to your actions. Whose actions will be as perfect as they need to be to achieve the goal which we established in previous verse.
One who is not attached to his actions. See, once Im attached to my actions -- I had an interview, I thought I did the best in my interview. Then this happens all the time.
When we go for an interview, we come back and they select us. How can they select him? I think we were the best team. Give us the feedback.
All of them are qualified. But what did we not do? You did everything right. But we thought the other day I was a little better than you are a little more appropriate for this project.
But we are so attached to our actions. We think that our actions are the most appropriate. Should get the result I am looking for.
But once I perform action, I should not be attached to Gata Sangasya. We are detached to your actions. Once you perform actions and move on, you are liberated from it.
You feel free because you are not thinking about it. Gnana Avasthita Cheta Saha. But this thing only came because Im established in knowledge. I have learned over and over and over again.
The results are not in my hand. Once that knowledge takes place that no matter how better I do, results will never be in my hand. Same presentation you make one time and you are the best.
And next time they will say you are the lowest. Gnana Vastyatchiyata Saha. His intellect is established in the knowledge that only control I have is on my own actions and not on the results. Yajnaya Acharataha Karma.
Therefore he is acting for only one reason.

Verse 22 presents the state we must achieve for perfect happiness: content with what comes without scheming (yadriccha-labha-santushtah), beyond the pairs of opposites (dvandvatitah), free from envy (vimatsarah), balanced in success and failure (samah siddhav asiddhau). Such a person, though acting, is not bound. Verse 23 shows the method: being free from attachment (gata-sangasya), liberated (muktasya), with mind established in knowledge (jnanaavasthita-chetasah), acting only for yajna - such a persons karma completely dissolves (samagram praviliyate).
The profound verse 24 reveals the ultimate vision: Brahmarpanam brahma havir brahmagnau brahmana hutam - the offering is Brahman, what is offered is Brahman, the fire is Brahman, the offerer is Brahman. When one sees this unity, even while acting, one remains united with God (brahmaiva tena gantavyam). This is like ice immersed in water - the cup, the water inside, and the water outside are all the same substance. The crystallization creates apparent separation, but upon melting, all is revealed as one.
Today, practice contentment with whatever comes naturally from your efforts, without manipulating results. When comparing yourself to others (a major source of suffering), remember vimatsarah - you do not know their full situation. What looks like success on social media hides struggles you cannot see. In your actions today, practice the Brahman vision: see the instrument of action (your body), the effort expended, the field of action, and the actor as expressions of one reality. When you fail or succeed, maintain samah siddhav asiddhau - equal-mindedness. Ask: If I truly believed that everything involved in my action is Brahman, how would I approach this task differently?
